access_note: Software free; some databases on openLCA Nexus are sold.
description: openLCA is a free, open-source life cycle assessment (LCA) and footprint software developed by GreenDelta in Berlin since 2006, which describes it as the most widely used LCA software. It models product systems at any level of complexity, links them to background databases, calculates impact assessment results and exports to many recognised formats, with libraries for fast calculation on large databases and Python (Jython) scripting. Version 2.7.0 is the current download for Windows, macOS and Linux (tested on Ubuntu 24.04), and the interface is translated into more than a dozen languages. The software is free with no hidden costs; many databases, some free and some for purchase, are offered on openLCA Nexus, and a free LCA Collaboration Server 2.0 and a commercial web tool, onlineLCA, support team work and mass calculation. Its global use covers industry, consulting and teaching. Users have no obligation to publish models or data built with it. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): MPL-2.0. Caveats: results depend heavily on the database chosen, and some databases are paid. For simulation it quantifies the life cycle emissions and resource use of infrastructure assets, materials and processes for decarbonisation and design comparisons. Related catalogue records include Brightway and EXIOBASE.
